solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old doublet in home nibbled at edge by pet?

indicators.note: something nibbled at its edge has lost a bit from its end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: your place is your home
a cat is a common pet

explanation.surface: An antique garment is found at home, its hem chewed by the family animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is only a link here, not a container signal: the shortened home simply comes before the pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A placcat (or placket) was an obsolete name for a doublet or stomacher, an archaic close-fitting garment.

clue.text: Spy chief and agent turning up in Russian city

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: M is the head of MI6 in the Bond novels
a rep is a sales agent

explanation.surface: The spymaster and an operative surface in a Russian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Perm is an industrial city in Russia, on the Kama River near the Urals.

clue.text: A very good name, not quite at the top spot

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
pi is short for pious, sanctimoniously very good
to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: A first-rate reputation, nearly reaching the number one position.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good.
explanation.definitionFit: Apical means relating to or situated at the apex, the tip or summit of something.

clue.text: Excellent copper to dash round end of street

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the word that follows
going round something puts it inside, surrounded

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to shy is to throw or fling, as to dash something
the final letter of street

explanation.surface: A great policeman rushes round the corner at the end of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer but gives the chemical symbol. Cushty is London slang, popularised by the sitcom Only Fools and Horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Cushty is British slang for very good or great, so a synonym for excellent.

clue.text: Oaf's inaccurate chatter could be of a ____ nature

definitions.text: Oaf's inaccurate chatter could be of a ____ nature

indicators.note: could be says one set of letters might be rearranged into another

blocks.note: all of these letters are the pool to rearrange
these letters are part of the rearranged pool and are taken away
these letters are also part of the pool and are taken away

explanation.surface: A clumsy man's careless talk might be described as having this quality.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus OF A NATURE uses exactly the letters of OAFS INACCURATE CHATTER, and the clue as a whole defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Catachrestic describes catachresis, the misuse of words, which is what an oaf's inaccurate talk shows.

clue.text: Hedgehog-like animals in a number of sports grounds

blocks.note: ten is a number
a rec is a recreation ground, the British term for a public playing field

explanation.surface: Spiny creatures turn up on several playing fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenrecs are small insectivores of Madagascar, many of them spiny and closely resembling hedgehogs.

clue.text: Music-maker cast out in our cellar, keeping noise to minimum

indicators.note: something cast out is thrown about, so these letters are scattered into a new order
reduced to a minimum, the word keeps only its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of noise

explanation.surface: A musician is thrown out of our cellar, told to keep the din down.
explanation.definitionFit: A carillonneur plays a carillon, a set of tuned bells, so he is a maker of music.

clue.text: Divine Scottish place deemed healthy by English

blocks.note: a spa town is visited for its supposedly healthy waters
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A Scottish resort is judged good for you by an English visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' is a verb, to foretell, not the adjective it seems; 'Scottish' tags the word as Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, to spae is to prophesy or foretell, which is what it means to divine.

clue.text: The old man is hanging around the Parisian dance-hall

indicators.note: hanging around something means surrounding it, so it goes inside

blocks.note: pa is a familiar word for father
taken as written
la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: Dad lingers near the dance hall in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old man' means father, not an elderly person, and 'hanging around' wraps the two words after it around the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: A palais (de danse) is a public dance hall, a word borrowed from French.

clue.text: Doctor I call before getting much-used antibiotic

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered in order

blocks.note: taken as written
something in is popular and much used

explanation.surface: A doctor says she calls before prescribing a popular antibiotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the caller in the surface but is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Allicin is the pungent compound in crushed garlic, which has antibacterial properties.

clue.text: Trade opportunity coming up to get neat new synthetic material

indicators.note: in a down answer, coming up means reading from the bottom upwards
new means made afresh, so these letters are given a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: a sale is an opportunity to trade
taken as written

explanation.surface: A business opening arises for a smart new man-made fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastane is a stretchy synthetic fibre, also called spandex or Lycra, a man-made textile.

clue.text: Catch the utterance of a wise person

indicators.note: the utterance of means the word as it is spoken, so its sound is what matters

blocks.note: a seer is a wise person who sees the future

explanation.surface: Listen carefully to what a sage says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' seems to mean hear but is a noun, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sear is the catch in a gunlock that holds the hammer cocked until the trigger is pulled.

clue.text: Plant with large sepal in very miserable state

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: in botany an ala is a wing, including a large lateral sepal
hell is a state of utter misery

explanation.surface: A flower with big sepals is in a sorry, wilting condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sepal' pulls you towards the definition, but the botanical term is wordplay; 'plant' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Heal-all is a common name for self-heal and other herbs credited with curing many ailments.

clue.text: Awkward sister refuses to move up north?

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsy disorder, so the letters are put out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A difficult sibling won't budge when the family heads north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up north' with its question mark flags a Scottish and northern dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Reist is a Scots verb used of a horse that balks and will not go forward, i.e. it refuses to move.

clue.text: Fish not initially seen in stream

indicators.note: not initially tells you to drop the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: the brill is a flatfish related to the turbot

explanation.surface: A fish not spotted at first in a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: A rill is a small brook or rivulet, so a stream in miniature.

clue.text: Sandy beach? Mum needs something to sit on

blocks.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
a chair is a seat

explanation.surface: At the seaside, mother wants a deckchair.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: machair is sandy coastal grassland in the Hebrides, not quite a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Machair is low-lying sandy land behind the shore in western Scotland, a near relative of a beach.

clue.text: Island, first to serve stale meals

indicators.note: first places the following piece before the island rather than after it

blocks.note: ka is an obsolete verb meaning to serve, as in 'ka me, ka thee'; stale marks it as no longer used
IS is a standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: On an island, the first thing to be served is old, dry food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stale' looks like it describes the meals but signals that the verb is obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Kai is a New Zealand word for food, so kais are meals or portions of food.

clue.text: Dishevelled woman to wander into valley

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

blocks.note: ratch is a dialect verb meaning to wander or ramble
a dell is a small wooded valley

explanation.surface: An untidy woman goes roaming off into the hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: A dratchell is a dialect word for a slattern, a slovenly or untidy woman.

clue.text: State of calm fellow about to enter boat

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it

blocks.note: a fellow is a man
c, for circa, means about
a dory is a small flat-bottomed boat

explanation.surface: A man at ease is about to climb into his boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' is not a reversal or a position here but C, short for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormancy is a state of rest or inactivity, a quiet suspended calm.

clue.text: Look for 'ollow space reportedly to get fuel

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so what counts is how the phrase sounds

blocks.note: to look for is to seek, and a hollow space is a hole, dropped-aitch style

explanation.surface: Search a cavity, said in a Cockney accent, to find some fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ollow tells you the H is dropped, so hole becomes 'ole.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea coal is coal washed up on beaches, or an old name for mined coal, both burnt as fuel.

clue.text: Antelopes and goats crossing wilderness initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
crossing something means straddling it, so it ends up inside

blocks.note: a lech is a lecher, figuratively a goat
the first letter of wilderness

explanation.surface: Herds of antelope and goats roam the wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goats' looks like animals beside the antelopes, but means lustful men.
explanation.definitionFit: The lechwe is an African antelope of swampy grasslands.

clue.text: Tree in that place to the west, one in America

indicators.note: in an across answer, heading west means reading leftwards, so backwards
one being in America means it is placed inside the abbreviation for that country

blocks.note: loc. cit., 'in the place cited', is abbreviated LC
I is the Roman numeral one
USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A tree grows somewhere off to the west, and one is found in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In that place' looks like plain English but is the scholarly loco citato, abbreviated LC.
explanation.definitionFit: Clusia is a genus of tropical American trees and shrubs, some known as balsam or autograph trees.

clue.text: Engineers facing tedious job, improvement to car engine

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a bore is a tedious task

explanation.surface: Mechanics face a tiresome task while upgrading a motor.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebore widens worn engine cylinders to restore performance, a standard overhaul for a car engine.

clue.text: Mineral no longer to pollute earth's surface

indicators.note: the surface of a word is its outermost top layer, so its first letter in a down answer

blocks.note: blend is an obsolete verb meaning to pollute or spoil
the first letter of earth

explanation.surface: A mineral that may no longer foul the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks the old sense of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Blende is zinc sulphide ore, also called sphalerite, a mineral.

clue.text: A biochemical substance that's no longer in appendages to organs

indicators.note: being in something means placed inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
DNA is deoxyribonucleic acid
ex means former, no longer

explanation.surface: A chemical no longer present in the body's attached parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Adnexa are structures attached to an organ, such as the ovaries and fallopian tubes beside the uterus.

clue.text: No sweet drink served up — one wants spirit

indicators.note: in a down answer, served up means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
mead is a sweet drink made from honey

explanation.surface: Offered no honey wine, someone wants hard liquor instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' looks like a drink, fitting the surface, but means a supernatural being.
explanation.definitionFit: A daemon is a spirit, in Greek myth a being between gods and humans.

clue.text: Somehow educate female about when ultimately to get pregnant

definitions.note: the answer is the transitive verb, to make pregnant

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are arranged in some unspecified new way
ultimately points to the very end of the word, its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female
the final letter of when

explanation.surface: Somehow explain the facts of life to a woman about when she will finally conceive.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a little loose: fecundate means to make pregnant or fertile, which 'get pregnant' can read as.
explanation.definitionFit: To fecundate is to make fruitful or impregnate, closely tied to conceiving a child.

clue.text: School expelling a triplet

indicators.note: expelling means throwing out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: to school someone is to train them
taken as written; this is the letter thrown out

explanation.surface: A school throws out one of three children born together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a noun but is the verb, to train.
explanation.definitionFit: Trin is a dialect word for one of three children born at one birth, a triplet.

clue.text: Tree, a sure thing to be cut down

indicators.note: cut down means shortened, so the last letter is chopped off

blocks.note: taken as written
a cert is a certainty, a sure thing

explanation.surface: A tree is certain to be felled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut down' suits a tree in the surface, but works on the sure thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the botanical genus of maples, so a tree.

clue.text: Place for chicks? Lustful king grabs one, expressing love

indicators.note: expressing here means pressing out, so the letter for love, a zero, is squeezed out
grabbing something means holding it, so it is placed inside

blocks.note: Henry VIII is famed for his six wives
taken as written

explanation.surface: A randy monarch seizes a girl while declaring his affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O, as the zero score in tennis; pressing it out of ONE leaves NE. 'Chicks' suggests girls but means young birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A hennery is a poultry farm or henhouse, where chickens are kept.

clue.text: Mountain creature not seen — one that's still on top?

indicators.note: in a down answer, on top means placed above, so the first piece sits over the second

blocks.note: yet means still, as in 'not yet'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An unseen beast of the peaks, one that is still at the summit?
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is the abominable snowman, a Himalayan creature that has never been reliably sighted.

clue.text: What you'd see in London street once, but not everywhere

indicators.note: what you would see in a phrase is something sitting inside its letters

blocks.note: spans the end of London and the start of street

explanation.surface: A street sign you might have spotted in London long ago, though not anywhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' looks like part of the surface's 'long ago' but is the definition; 'not everywhere' marks a regional form.
explanation.definitionFit: Onst is a dialect form of once, used only in some regions, hence not everywhere.

clue.text: Hysterical type, the first person to be heard repeatedly

indicators.note: to be heard means what counts is how the words sound when spoken

blocks.note: the first person is me, said twice over
no letters of its own: it says the pronoun is spoken more than once

explanation.surface: An attention-seeker is the first to be heard again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' doubles the pronoun; a self-absorbed 'me, me' fits the surface picture of someone hysterical.
explanation.definitionFit: A meemie is a hysterical person, as in the 'screaming meemies', a fit of nervous hysteria.

clue.text: Bad man stopped working and went on a course to be helpful

definitions.text: went on a course to be helpful

blocks.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
a machine that died stopped working

explanation.surface: A scoundrel broke down and then took a course in being useful.
explanation.walkthrough: The course is a golf course, not a training class.
explanation.definitionFit: To caddie is to carry a golfer's clubs round the course, helping the player.

clue.text: See about getting marks for supposedly original material

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word is read the other way

blocks.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is a cathedral city and see
M is the abbreviation for the German mark

explanation.surface: Look around to find marks on what is said to be an original document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Ylem is the hypothetical primordial matter from which the elements were formed, hence supposedly original.

clue.text: Instrument made a sound, interrupting monkey

indicators.note: something interrupting another breaks into the middle of it

blocks.note: a bell rang, making a sound
the sai is a South American capuchin monkey

explanation.surface: A musical instrument sounded, disturbing a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The sarangi is a bowed stringed instrument of North India.
